message.content: We're seeing a 1500-line PR for the V31 schema migration. Should it be split per our 1000-LoC cap?

The 1000-LoC cap was set in 2025-Q2 to keep feature reviews tractable. The reasoning was that beyond ~1000 LoC the reviewer's context window for design intent collapses. Migration PRs are different in nature — most of the touch is mechanical (schema bump, prepared-statement updates) where the reviewer's cognitive load isn't dominated by design judgement.
So you're saying the rule shouldn't apply mechanically?

Exactly. The rule's framework is review-tractability. For migration PRs, tractability comes from a different axis: did the schema diff land cleanly, did the prepared-statement updates compile, did the down-migration test pass. A 1500-line migration PR with three tightly-related concerns is more tractable than a 900-line feature PR with five subtly-coupled concerns.
Concretely, what would you propose for migration PRs?

Migration-specific gates: (1) the schema diff is reviewable in isolation; (2) every code site touched is prepared-statement-bound (no business logic); (3) the down-migration is included and tested. If those three hold, the PR is tractable regardless of LoC. The 1000-LoC cap should be flagged as feature-PR-only in the policy text.
OK, let's update the policy to scope the cap to feature work and add the migration-specific gates.
Will draft the policy update. The core insight: LoC is a proxy for cognitive load that breaks down when work is mechanical. Different categories of PR need different tractability gates.
